Constructionist social problems theory argues that social problems are best understood as processes: they emerge when people define certain conditions as troubling and make claims to persuade others that action is needed. Despite this focus on claimsmaking, relatively little attention has been devoted to how analysts decide which claims warrant investigation. We argue that analysts are often drawn to what we term “the gap”: a disconnect between what is being claimed and the evidence available to assess those claims.

This article examines how Vladimir Putin constructs Russia as a state-civilisation through strategic rhetoric that combines Aristotelian enthymematic reasoning with selective historical narratives. The analysis identifies three interrelated enthymemes that underpin Putin’s civilisational narrative.
